{/* Main Thesis Card */}
┌─[ Undergraduate Thesis — BRAC University ]

$ 3C-Net: Cervical Cancer Cell Classification using Deep Learning

For my undergraduate thesis at BRAC University, I developed 3C-Net — a lightweight convolutional neural network designed to automatically classify cervical cells from Liquid-Based Cytology (LBC) Pap smear images into four clinical categories: HSIL, LSIL, NILM, and SCC.

Outperforms established architectures including VGG-19, ResNet-50, EfficientNet, and DenseNet-121 on the same dataset.

$ explainability --methods

To ensure clinical trustworthiness, I integrated Explainable AI techniques — Grad-CAM and LIME — that visually highlight which regions of each cell image drove the model's decision.

{/* Impact Statement */}
🎯

The goal was to build a practical, resource-efficient diagnostic aid that can support early cervical cancer detection in low-resource healthcare settings.
